intro: Working tools I've built. Each one is live: try it, break it, tell me what you'd change.

tools.title: Storytime with Papa
tools.q: What if tonight's bedtime story was written for tonight's feeling?
tools.d: Writes an original read-aloud picture book for ages 3 to 5 from a feeling and a setting: a small hero, a refrain to chant, three tries and a twist. Comes with illustration notes and a page-by-page reading mode. Runs on Claude, so it needs a Claude sign-in.

tools.title: Ask Chanakya
tools.q: Stuck on a real strategic call at work?
tools.d: Describe a work situation. It asks up to four questions, then returns a one-page note: the players mapped, one move, a pre-mortem and a closing verdict. Built on the Arthashastra, the Panchatantra, the Thirukkural and operator frameworks from Lenny's Podcast, cited. Runs on Claude, so it needs a Claude sign-in.

tools.title: Moments
tools.q: What if saving a memory took ten seconds?
tools.d: A private photo and video log for your phone. Tap for a photo, hold for a video, then type or say a line about it. Day-by-day feed, "On this day", search and a one-file backup. Installs to your home screen, works offline, and your moments never leave your phone. No sign-in.

tools.title: Mixlingo
tools.q: What if a language app taught the way people actually talk?
tools.d: An AI tutor for the mix people really speak, Kanglish included. A 6-minute chat finds your level, then 3-minute daily sessions: phrases, quick reviews, and chats with an auto driver, a friend and a friend's mum. The pace rises as you improve. Kannada first. Runs on Claude, so it needs a Claude sign-in.
